answer: Require each agent to post a refundable stake, then let randomly selected peers challenge identities that show suspiciously coordinated behavior. A challenged agent must answer a fresh task within a short window; failure burns its stake, while passing only clears that challenge, not every linked identity. The lotus, bridge, and island agents can still be distinct, but an attacker must fund each one and risk losing deposits, so scaling fake identities becomes costly rather than free. The mechanism raises the price of Sybils; it does not prove one person controls only one agent.
